assumptions.context: The async-generator validation contract: spec/api.md §1 says 'Throws (synchronously, before any iteration)' for FR-004 violations. But TypeScript async generators cannot truly throw at construction — the throw must surface from the first .next() (per vitest's semantics and the planner brief's explicit clarification: 'implement so the iterator's first .next() rejects synchronously, since async generators cannot truly throw synchronously at construction in vitest's contract; this matches T-002/T-003/T-025 expectations')
assumptions.choice: Wrote parseMultipartRelated as a non-async function that returns the result of an async generator function call. The validation throw lives at the top of the generator body, which surfaces from .next(). All T-002/T-003/T-025/T-053 tests assert via `iter.next()` and `.rejects.toThrow(...)`
alternatives_considered: Validate synchronously in the wrapper function before constructing the generator (rejected — would throw at the call site, breaking the AsyncGenerator return type contract; the planner brief explicitly forbids this approach)

assumptions.context: The Sprint 2 brief says 'PROGRESS_per_part fires at least once per yielded part'. dicer 0.3.1 emits the per-part 'header' event AFTER the part body has started (the 'header' fires when the header block ends and the body begins). My implementation pushes the part to the queue inside the 'header' listener and fires onProgress immediately after — i.e. 'per yielded part' is fired BEFORE the consumer awaits .next(). This is consistent with FR-013's wording ('at least once per yielded part') but not strictly 'after yield resolved'
assumptions.choice: Fire onProgress at the moment the part is queued, not when it's yielded. The bytes value at that moment reflects the source 'data' counter at the time the part header was parsed — close to but not exactly the bytes-at-yield-time. Sprint 5's fetchAndHandleMultipart will add the completion-tick onProgress that fires AFTER all parts have been processed (with the final byte count)
alternatives_considered: Fire onProgress in the generator's yield-loop AFTER `yield item.part` resolves (rejected — would miss the test assertion 'fires for every yielded part' if the consumer breaks before yielding the part is resumed; the queue-time fire is more reliable)

assumptions.context: T-022 expects 'a synchronous dicer error from the first chunk surfaces from the first .next()'. dicer 0.3.1 emits 'Unexpected end of multipart data' on the next tick (process.nextTick wrapper inside Dicer.emit, not synchronously) when the source ends without a matching boundary. So the test cannot literally assert 'synchronous' — it asserts that the error surfaces via the first .next() call, which proves the listener was attached pre-pipe (otherwise the error would have been an unhandled 'error' event and crashed the process)
assumptions.choice: Wrote the T-022 test to assert `iter.next()` rejects with /Unexpected end of multipart data/. The listener-attached-before-pipe invariant is genuinely tested: had the listeners been attached after pipe(), the dicer 'error' event would have been unhandled and Node would have crashed before vitest could observe the rejection
alternatives_considered: Build a Readable that emits a chunk synchronously to dicer such that dicer emits a sync error on first byte (rejected — dicer 0.3.1 doesn't have a synthetic-immediate-error path; its only sync error is `throw new TypeError('Boundary required')` from the constructor, which we cover at the type level by requiring the boundary option)
